people.name: Hara Prasad Shastri
people.field: Sanskrit scholar, archivist, and historian of Bengali literature

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: Shastri initially studied at the village school and then at Sanskrit College and Presidency College in Calcutta

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: Shastri initially studied at the village school and then at Sanskrit College and Presidency College in Calcutta (now Kolkata)... received a BA in 1876

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: He then joined Hare School as a teacher in 1878.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: He became a professor at the Sanskrit College in 1883.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: In 1895, he headed the Sanskrit department at Presidency College.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: During the winter 1898–99, he assisted Dr. Cecil Bendall during research in Nepal, collecting information from the private Durbar Library

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: He became Principal of Sanskrit College in 1900, leaving in 1908 to join the government's Bureau of Information.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.role: Professor and Head of the Department of Bengali and Sanskrit
relations.evidence: From 1921 to 1924, he was Professor and Head of the Department of Bengali and Sanskrit at Dhaka University.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: Shastri held different positions within the Asiatic Society, and was its president for two years.

relations.subject: Hara Prasad Shastri
relations.evidence: He was also President of Bangiya Sahitya Parishad for twelve years

relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who was a friend of Shastri's older brother, Nandakumar Nyayachunchu
